messages.subject: valid weartime
parts:
Hello,

I have a question regarding number of hrs of valid weartime.  It seems that the threshold for including/excluding days of based on hours of valid weartime might be different based on what you are studying (ie sleep vs PA) and based on when the nonweartime occurred (e.g sleep window vs nonsleep window).  We asked participants to wear 24 hrs a day and have a pretty small sample.  Right now just 59 people but by the end of the study hopefully 320.  We want to assess inactive and PA time, and also assess measures of sleep quality.  Can you give any guidance on how to set thresholds for weartime?  

thanks

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] valid weartime
parts:
The default GGIR settings should be reasonable for most purposes. The part 2 analysis will by default require at least 16 hours of valid data per day (midnight-midnight) while the sleep analysis require the same number of valid hours for thewindow defined from noon-noon. In part 5 the day time inclusion criteria is by default 2/3 of the waking hours. I would not recommend lowering these values. The literature about a minimum of 10 valid hours per day was done in studies where the accelerometer was not supposed to be worn during the night. That strongly affects the interpretation of non-wear time and makes it incompatible with a 24 hour protocol.

Deciding on non-wear threshold consider:
- believes about what represents a valid day for each of the outcomes measures.
- demographics of (in)valid data in your study population.

Vincent
